approach.method_basis: The Parent is a graph-based genetic algorithm that picks its offspring by Gaussian-process Thompson sampling. Each round of ten, it breeds a fresh pool of 160 candidate molecules from a 64-molecule elite. Breeding parents come mostly from the top score quantiles. An offspring is made either by joining connected fragments of two parents, sometimes followed by one more edit, or by a short chain of atom, bond and ring edits. Duplicates are rejected. So is any offspring that would introduce a sulfur environment its scored parents do not already contain. A Gaussian process scores the whole pool in advance. It is trained on every molecule scored so far in the run, using count-based Morgan fingerprints and a Tanimoto-type similarity. Ten correlated samples are drawn from its posterior, each sample picks its best remaining candidate, and those ten molecules are scored. Two separate random-number generators drive a run. One makes every breeding decision: which parents, crossover or mutation, how many edits and which ones. The other draws only the posterior samples.
approach.novelty: This arm adds no new search behaviour. It is a placebo that measures how far luck alone moves the scores when a whole run takes a different random path. At the start of every round, before any breeding, it draws one number from the breeding generator and throws it away. From the very first round, every later breeding decision therefore uses a different random draw. The pools, the scored molecules and the elite all drift away from the Parent's run, while every rule, probability and threshold stays exactly the same, and so do the selector's own random numbers. The two earlier placebos on this Parent changed only the selector's random numbers, and only after a run had gone three rounds without improving. They never touched the two deco_hop runs that never stall, so they can only calibrate changes gated on that stall signal. The 28 whole-run changes tried on this Parent also leave its path in round one, but each of them changes a rule at the same time, and all 28 lost one unusually lucky deco_hop result. This arm departs in the same way without changing any rule. It therefore shows what departure alone costs, including whether that lucky result survives a re-draw.

observed_bottleneck: Ungated whole-run contrasts on this Anchor have no law-free reference. All 28 complete ungated Children of n-1744a1494180 leave its path at the first announced batch, and all 28 are negative against it (mean -0.061895; mildest n-5cc22bb8f56b -0.013060 and n-da0eeecfb462 -0.016060; also n-c070e95b09ef -0.030700, n-9d88f032c4dc -0.038955, n-37a4fc183d94 -0.055187). Every one of them loses the inherited deco_hop seed-0 endpoint 0.856148 and lands between 0.581 and 0.635, which costs about -0.016 of a fifteen-cell mean. That endpoint comes from a single best-so-far jump from 0.609560 at evaluation 280 to 0.856148 at evaluation 281, and the trajectory is byte-identical since n-62daf219c70a. All ten stall-gated Children keep the endpoint, because deco_hop seeds 0 and 2 never stall. The only two law-free references perturb only the allocator torch stream, and only from each session's first stalled batch: R1 n-47993ce5d053 (-0.001735) and R2 n-843b25e73dee (+0.007747). Neither touches the breeding random.Random stream, and neither exposes deco_hop seeds 0 and 2. The goal's review condition therefore treats every ungated delta as uncalibrated, including this round's ungated position. The registered deco_hop departure obstacle also cannot yet be assigned either to the frozen panel and its selected realization or to the mechanisms tested.
hypothesis: Law-free breeding-stream path divergence. At the start of every announced batch, before that batch's GP fit and its first breeding decision, draw exactly one value with random() from the Evolution's own seeded random.Random generator and discard it. GraphOperators shares this generator, so it drives quantile parent and rank sampling, the crossover-versus-mutation coin, the post-crossover finishing coin, the ordinary walk-length draw and every operator, site and element draw. The discard changes which pseudo-random words all later breeding decisions consume, from the first announced batch of every session. Offspring pools, emitted molecules, the accepted archive and survivors therefore diverge from the Anchor's realization. Every law is unchanged: probabilities, thresholds, operator menu, escalation, sulfur gate, identity admission and both duplicate scopes, pool target, accepted-only count-GP fit, and correlated Thompson allocation. The allocator's separately seeded torch generator still draws one (10, 160) block per batch, so its standard-normal rows stay bitwise equal to the Anchor's. The claim is about a measurement, not a gain. This one change moves the realized breeding path in all fifteen sessions, including deco_hop seeds 0 and 2. Its complete matched panel delta is what path departure alone costs on this Anchor, and it is the reference band for ungated whole-run contrasts.

finding_summary.headline: Luck-only breeding re-draw cost -0.0099 on the panel and lost the lucky 0.856 deco_hop cell like all 28 rule changes; median_2 moved -0.0005
finding_summary.insights:
Pure path luck, with no rule changed, produces the same signature as all 28 earlier whole-run rule changes on this Parent. It loses the 0.856 deco_hop seed-0 endpoint, landing at 0.611, inside the 0.581-0.635 range of those 28. It also loses the 0.694 sitagliptin seed-0 endpoint, which all 28 fall below as well. Both cells are favourable draws of the Parent's own run, not damage done by the rule changes. The deco_hop must-preserve margin is therefore breached by departure alone. Any change that leaves the Parent's path early should be expected to lose about 0.08 on the deco_hop task mean, whatever it does. That is a property of the frozen panel for the human to weigh; it does not relax the margin or exclude the cell. The chemistry fits this reading. The re-drawn deco_hop seed-0 session ran away into roughly 1,100-Da peroxide-linked polyaromatics, and 269 of its crossover attempts produced no molecule, consistent with the 120-atom cap on two parents of that size. The two sessions that stayed small reached higher endpoints. Which path a run happens to take decides this cell.

The cell spread makes the pre-registered reading band wide: R3 = -0.0099 with half-width 0.0410. An ungated panel now stands above the law-free reference only above +0.0311 and below it only under -0.0509. Of the 28 earlier ungated changes, 13 fall below (-0.183 to -0.052) and 15 cannot be told apart from luck (-0.051 to -0.013, including the two mildest); none stands above. So 'all 28 negative' is roughly half harm beyond path luck and half the ordinary cost of leaving the Parent's path. The median_2 band is narrower: R3 = -0.0005 with half-width 0.0072, so above +0.0067 or below -0.0078. Five earlier ungated changes clear its upper edge by 0.002 to 0.005 (largest +0.0120), 10 fall below and 13 sit inside. Those five are leads, not achievements. This is one dependent draw, the median_2 floor width was borrowed from the stall-gated controls, and luck alone has moved single median_2 cells by up to 0.006 here and 0.029 in an earlier control. Median_2 also showed its plateau again: this run's seed-2 best and the first selector control's seed-2 best are different molecules with exactly the same score, 0.227237.

The design assumed that one discarded number would shift every later breeding draw. At the level of raw random words that is false. Python's rejection sampling can re-synchronize two streams within a draw, and on all three seeds it did so inside the very first parent draw. On seed 1 the one decision made before re-synchronization still differed, and that was enough. On seeds 0 and 2 nothing in round 1 changed. The reference is still ungated, and every session left the Parent's path by evaluation 32, long before the evaluation-281 jump. Its whole-run calibration therefore stands. A design that needs a guaranteed round-one departure would have to re-seed the breeding generator rather than discard a value. The route's review condition rules out a second ungated draw, so this is recorded only as design knowledge.

Still open: this is one realization. It is coupled to the Parent through the identical selector stream and the re-synchronized breeding stream, so it bounds the size of path noise without estimating it, and no significance statement follows. The round's own ungated position was still running when this brief was written, so applying the band to it is left to Curate.
finding_summary.results:
The control ran as registered. In all 15 sessions the run drew and threw away one breeding random number at the start of each of its 29 rounds (435 in total). Each discard came before that round's model fit and first breeding step, and the round-1 values were exactly the predicted ones for each seed. No other rule moved. The selector's own random numbers matched the Parent's bit for bit in all 4,350 picks. Every pool held 160 candidates and no round used the backup route. The model's training sets and normalization matched the inherited rule, and its predictions recomputed to within 5e-14. Operator frequencies, the crossover rate (45.1%) and the finishing rate (35.6%) sat within their nominal bands. The selected candidates also sat at the same places in the predicted-score and uncertainty rankings as the Parent's: shift statistics +0.03 and +0.24, far inside the 3.26 bound.

The path departed in every session, but in ten of them later than registered. On seed 1 all five sessions changed their very first breeding decision, and their round-1 pools shared only 137 to 159 of 160 candidates with the Parent's. On seeds 0 and 2 the two runs made identical decisions within that first parent draw. Python draws random integers by rejecting and redrawing some random words. The Parent's run happened to spend extra words on rejections at exactly that point, which absorbed the two words the discard had used. Round 1 therefore came out identical molecule for molecule. Those ten sessions departed at a later discard instead: round 2 in nine of them and round 3 in drd2_docking seed 0. Their first differing scored molecule came at evaluation 21 to 32, not 11. After the split the runs were as far apart as any rule change. Only 2.3% of the molecules scored after the split also appear in the Parent's same session; the round-38 rule changes ranged from 2.3% to 6.1%.

Scores: the panel mean was 0.586565 against the Parent's 0.596453, a reference delta of -0.009888. Seed macros moved -0.0671, +0.0314 and +0.0060. Six cells rose and nine fell, with a wide spread (cell SD 0.079). Two cells dominate. Deco_hop seed 0 fell from 0.856 to 0.611 (-0.245), and sitagliptin seed 1 rose from 0.500 to 0.657 (+0.157). Without deco_hop seed 0, the other fourteen cells average +0.0069. The Parent's 0.856148 deco_hop seed-0 endpoint was not reproduced. This run's best-so-far there was 0.6073 at evaluation 200 and 0.6112 from evaluation 265 onward, including evaluations 280, 281 and 300. The Parent was at 0.6096 at evaluation 280 and jumped to 0.8561 at evaluation 281. That one cell costs -0.0163 of the panel mean, inside the predicted -0.014 to -0.018. Sitagliptin seed 0 also fell, from 0.694 to 0.599.

For the Research Brief, the median_2 three-seed mean went from 0.222732 to 0.222196 (-0.0005), with cells -0.0024, +0.0058 and -0.0051. On the protected tasks, drd2_docking (+0.0057), sitagliptin_mpo (+0.0335) and zaleplon_mpo (-0.0083) stay within their margins. Deco_hop falls by 0.0798, far beyond its 0.02 margin, and all of that loss comes from the seed-0 cell (seeds 1 and 2 moved +0.0105 and -0.0050). Against the two earlier luck-only controls, which perturbed only the selector and only after a stall, this panel is 0.0082 and 0.0176 lower.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic cores decorated with N-F, N-O and peroxide bonds; one session ran away to 1100 Da polyaromatics, and nothing carries defined stereochemistry.
molecular.overall_character: I read the digest and then all fifteen Child trajectory files in focus.artifacts.this_node_trajectories (three seeds x five objectives, 300 records each: ten initial and 290 optimizer proposals per session, 4350 optimizer molecules in total, all 4350 RDKit-parseable) and all fifteen published Parent trajectories for n-1744a1494180 in focus.artifacts.parent_trajectories. Every one of those thirty paths exists and was read; context.molecular_digest.tasks_without_trajectories is empty, so no objective is omitted and no path is missing. context.comparison reports child_complete true and paired_complete true on matched seeds 0/1/2 against code Parent n-1744a1494180, so each Parent contrast below is a complete-pairing chemical observation and never a score, ranking or activation claim. cited_smiles are restricted to molecules I verified by re-reading context.citation_trajectory_paths; Parent molecules are described numerically in prose only. The output is uniformly ring-rich and aromatic, consistent with the digest counters: ring_closure_rate 0.9552-0.9885 and aromatic_atom_rate 0.9471-0.9782 on every task, and my RDKit reading of the same files gives a median of 3-6 rings and 1-3 aromatic rings per molecule. The ring inventory is 11718 six-membered and 3712 five-membered rings, but also 2030 four-membered rings (1455 molecules contain one) and 1065 molecules carrying a ring of seven atoms or more, up to fourteen. Common saturated medicinal rings are nearly absent: of 4350 molecules, piperazine appears in 17, morpholine in 1 and piperidine in 168. Size is task-dependent and poorly controlled: median heavy atoms are 24, 41, 32, 31 and 27 by task, but a single deco_hop session drifted to a median of 72 heavy atoms and 978 Da over its whole run. The recurring chemical signature is heteroatom-heteroatom bonding, which a chemist would object to in most of these settings: 38.1 percent of the 4350 molecules carry an N-O, N-N, N-S or O-O single bond, 19.3 percent carry a halogen bonded to nitrogen, 6.5 percent carry a peroxide and 11.9 percent a free thiol. Not one of the 4350 molecules carries a trifluoromethyl group, a formal charge (digest charged_rate 0.0 on all five tasks) or a single stereochemical descriptor, while 2540 of them contain at least one unassigned sp3 stereocentre. Two of the five sets, median_2 and zaleplon_mpo, sit closest to ordinary medicinal chemistry on size and QED; the deco_hop set is the farthest from it.

per_task.generated_character: Small and conventional in size: median 24 heavy atoms, MW about 340-350, median 3 rings and 3 aromatic rings, fsp3 0.17, median SA score 3.06 and the lowest of the five sets. The dominant motif on seeds 1 and 2 is a fused bicyclic heteroaromatic bearing an aryl or 3-pyridyl carboxamide, decorated with methyl, methoxy and vinyl, as in C=Cc1c(C)c(C)cc2[nH]c(C(=O)N(O)c3cccnc3)cc12 at 0.4606 and C=Cc1c(OC)c(C)cc2[nH]c(C(=O)N(S)c3cccnc3)cc12 at 0.4598. Seed 0 settled on a different core, an N-bridged pyrazolo system carrying an exocyclic amidine, Cc1c(OCO)cc2c(cc3n2N=C3C(=N)c2ccccc2)c1C at 0.4573, with hemiacetal-like OCO and OCS side chains. Digest halogen_rate is 0.7195 and mean SMILES length 41.1.
liabilities: N-hydroxy anilide C(=O)N(O) in the best molecule of the task, an N-oxidised amide rather than a stable hydroxamic acid
N-sulfanyl amide C(=O)N(S); free thiol in 34.4 percent of the task's 870 molecules
hemiacetal-like OCO and OCS side chains on an aromatic oxygen, which would not survive isolation
exocyclic C(=N)H amidine on the seed-0 core, with acyclic imines in 60 percent of that session's proposals
halogen bonded to nitrogen in 9.9 percent of the task's molecules
degenerate one- and three-atom proposals consuming oracle evaluations at the 0.0 floor
missing_features: no nitrile anywhere in the 60 highest-scoring molecules and only 3 of 870 overall, although the set otherwise builds nitrogen-rich aromatics
no trifluoromethyl or other polyfluorinated carbon group in any of the 870 molecules
no tertiary N,N-dialkyl amide in the top 60, and only 0.9 percent of the whole set
no basic amine on a saturated ring in the top 60 (1.7 percent) although 8.3 percent of the whole set carries a basic amine
no defined stereochemistry, and no sp3-rich saturated ring to carry it: fsp3 median 0.16-0.22
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The gradient rewards holding one fused bicyclic heteroaromatic with an N-aryl carboxamide at roughly 24 heavy atoms and varying only its small substituents. Median block score rises from 0.228 at evaluations 11-40 to about 0.37-0.40 by evaluation 220 while median heavy atoms never leave 23-25, so the gain is decoration, not growth. Best-so-far then plateaus: 0.457 by evaluation 202 on seed 0 and 0.460 by 221 on seed 1, with no further movement in the last eighty evaluations. The low end is purely degenerate: C=CCl, NOO and O score exactly 0.0, and 36 of the 870 molecules have five or fewer heavy atoms.

per_task.generated_character: The largest and least drug-like set, and the only one where the three sessions diverged in size. Over all 870 molecules the median is 41 heavy atoms with median SA score 4.35, and the digest records mean SMILES length 86.9 and max 224. Seed 0 ran away: median 72 heavy atoms and 978 Da across its whole run, and its 30 best molecules average 85 heavy atoms, MW 1136, 10 rings, 10 aromatic rings and QED 0.03. Those molecules are two or three theophylline-like dimethylpyrimidinedione-fused pyrroles strung together through a peroxide O-O linker and capped with an ynol ether, as in C#COC=Cc1cc(-n2cc3c(c2C(=C)C=CC=C)c(=O)n(C)c(=O)n3C)nc2nc(OOc3cc4nc(C(=C)C=CC(=C)C)cc(-n5cc6c(c5C)c(=O)n(C)c(=O)n6C(=O)SC#C)c4cc3C)ccc12 at 0.6112; peroxide and alkyne each appear in 100 percent of that session's top 30. Seeds 1 and 2 stayed at 41 and 30 median heavy atoms and produced the digest best, C#COC(=O)c1c(CC)c(C(N=CC)Nc2nc3c(F)cc2-3)c2c(c1OC)CCC=N2 at 0.6392, a propiolate ester on a dihydroquinoline-like core linked to a strained fused azirine.
liabilities: peroxide O-O in 28.7 percent of the task's molecules and in 100 percent of the runaway session's top 30; a diaryl peroxide of this size is not a makeable compound
ynol ether C#C-O in 41 percent of that session's proposals, a functional group with essentially no synthetic precedent
MW above 1100 with QED 0.03 and median logP 6.97 in the top 30 of that session
cumulated polyene chains C(=C)C=CC=C appended to aromatic rings
strained fused azirine in the best molecules of seed 2, written as nc3c(F)cc2-3
fragments as small as C#C and FCl evaluated at the 0.5 objective floor
missing_features: no compact drug-sized replacement core on the runaway session: its top 30 never fall below about 70 heavy atoms, while the other two sessions scored higher at 30-41
no basic amine and no saturated N-heterocycle in the 60 highest-scoring molecules (0 of 60), although 21.7 percent of the task's molecules carry a saturated N-heterocycle
no amide NH in the top 60 and only 1.7 percent of the whole set, so hydrogen-bond donors are absent at the top (median HBD 0)
no defined stereochemistry at any of the many sp3 centres the fused cores create
no trifluoromethyl group in any of the 870 molecules
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The gradient here is nearly flat and generously floored, which is what the molecules show. The digest span is best 0.6392, median 0.600608, worst 0.5000, and bare fragments collect exactly 0.5: C#C, CCF, CC#N, OF, FCl and C1#COOC1 all score 0.5. The whole 300-evaluation search therefore moves roughly 0.1, and seed 0 bought its share by accumulating mass: median heavy atoms rise from 38 at evaluations 11-40 to 110 at 131-160 while median block score moves only 0.559 to 0.602. Seeds 1 and 2 reached higher endpoints (0.631 and 0.639) at a third of the molecular weight, so size was not what the objective rewarded. On the paired Parent run, seed 0 reaches 0.856148 at evaluation 281 with a 27-heavy-atom bicyclic (read from runs/SPIRAL2/nodes/n-1744a1494180/seed-0/trajectories/deco_hop.jsonl); this Child's seed-0 session never exceeded 0.6112 and never proposed a molecule of that compact class.

per_task.generated_character: The most sp3-rich and the most recognisably pharmacological set: median 32 heavy atoms, MW 470-535, median 2 aromatic rings but 2-6 rings in total, fsp3 0.37-0.50, digest halogen_rate 0.9874. This is the one objective where the generator reliably builds a basic nitrogen: 78.9 percent of the 870 molecules and 100 percent of the 60 highest-scoring carry a basic amine, 59.2 percent carry it on a ring, and all of the top 60 contain a saturated N-heterocycle. The best molecule, CCC(Cl)c1cc(F)cc(CCCC2CCCN2C23CN2c2cc(Cl)ccc23)c1 at 0.99999, is a 2-substituted pyrrolidine whose nitrogen is tied into a spiro aziridine-indoline, with a three-carbon linker to a chloro-fluoro arene. Seed 1 found a different and more linear answer, COc1cc(F)cc(CCNCC(NS(=O)c2cccc(Br)c2)C2(F)CCN2C)c1N at 0.9970, and seed 2 a fused indoline bearing a spiro azetidinyl-prolinamine with a chlorophenol biaryl, CN1c2cc(-c3cc(O)cc(Cl)c3)cc3c2C1C(C1(N2CCC2)CCCN1)C3CN at 0.9931.
liabilities: aziridine or azetidine in 78 percent of seed 0's and 64 percent of seed 2's proposals and in 100 percent of both sessions' top 30; the best molecule reaches its basic nitrogen through an N-aryl aziridine
spiro aminal nitrogen-carbon-nitrogen centres at the ring fusion, hydrolytically fragile as drawn
halogen bonded to nitrogen in 10.6 percent and alpha-halo amine in 9-10 percent of the set
pendant primary CH2NH2 handles left unelaborated on the top seed-2 molecules
median logP 5.3-5.9 with MW near 490 in the higher-scoring blocks
three to four unassigned stereocentres per molecule in the top 30
missing_features: almost no six-membered aromatic nitrogen in the top 60 (1.7 percent), so the aryl half is carbocyclic where a pyridine-type ring would be ordinary
no piperazine: 17 molecules in the node's entire 4350, and none in this task's top 60, although a ring basic nitrogen is exactly what the gradient rewards
no amide and no sulfonamide in the top 60, despite sulfonamide appearing in 13.2 percent of the whole set
no trifluoromethyl group in any of the 870 molecules
no stereochemical specification at a median of 3-4 stereocentres per molecule, so the proposals do not name the enantiomer the pocket would select
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The gradient tracks one pharmacophore: a basic nitrogen on a saturated ring joined by a two- or three-carbon linker to a halogenated aromatic. Median block score climbs from 0.029 to 0.968 on seed 0 while median heavy atoms fall from 40 to 29, so the search won by trimming and by installing the amine, not by growing. Basic-amine incidence is 78.9 percent over the set but 100 percent in the top 60, and the worst molecules are the inherited sulfonamide and plain-arene fragments: O=C(NCl)C1CCCN1S(=O)(=O)c1cc(Cl)cc(Cl)c1 at 0.000167 and CCc1cccc(Cl)c1 at 0.0026, both without a basic centre. The digest span, best 0.99999 and median 0.743514, is the widest of the five tasks.

per_task.generated_character: The most conventional-looking set of the five: median 31 heavy atoms, MW about 420, 4-6 rings, median 2 aromatic rings, fsp3 0.35-0.43 and median QED 0.56-0.71. Digest halogen_rate is only 0.108, the lowest of the five tasks, so these are halogen-free polar heterocycles. The dominant motif is a 2-alkylquinoline carrying an ethoxy enol ether fused into an N-methyl imide ring, as in CCCc1cc(C2C(OCC)=C3CC(=O)N(C)C(=O)N(CCN2C)C3)c2ccccc2n1 at 0.2272 and the seed-1 best CCCc1nc2cc(c1OCC)C1C(=O)N(C)CC3=C(CC3N1C)c1ccccc1O2 at 0.2272. Tertiary amide appears in 98.3 percent and imide in 76.7 percent of the 60 highest-scoring molecules, and a six-membered aromatic nitrogen in 96.7 percent.
liabilities: N-O single bonds in 70 percent of seed 0's proposals and 83 percent of its top 30, for example CCc1c2ccc(OCCc3cc(C)nc4ccccc34)c1C(N1CCC3NN(O1)C3=O)CC(=O)N2C, which also carries a ring hydrazine
hydrazine N-N in 30 percent of seed 0's and 13 percent of seed 2's proposals
four-membered rings in 55 percent of seed 0's and 60 percent of seed 1's proposals
N-S single bonds, as in CCCc1cc(SN2CCN3CC(=C(OCC)N2Br)C(=O)N(C)C3=O)c2ccccc2n1, where an N-Br also appears
median SA score 4.6-5.3 with bridged bicyclics that would be slow to make
missing_features: no carboxylic acid (3 of 870) and no sulfonamide (1 of 870), so the set carries no acidic or strongly polar anionic handle
no trifluoromethyl group and essentially no halogen at all: digest halogen_rate 0.108
no defined stereochemistry, although the fused and bridged cores carry a median of 2-3 stereocentres each
no biaryl linkage in the top 60 (0 of 60) against 11.6 percent of the whole set
no basic amine in the top 30 of the Parent-matched seed-0 session beyond ring nitrogens already tied into imides
per_task.score_gradient_reading: This gradient is extremely compressed and the molecules show why the search cannot read it: the digest span is best 0.2272 against median 0.18795, and best-so-far creeps from 0.168 to 0.227 across all 300 evaluations, about 0.06 for the whole run. What separates high from low is retaining the three-part quinoline plus ethoxy plus N-methyl imide motif while bridging an extra ring onto it; median heavy atoms drift only 31 to 37 on seed 0 and the score follows 0.149 to 0.198. Degenerate fragments S, C and NNO sit at 0.0, and only 8 of the 870 molecules fall below six heavy atoms, the cleanest of the five sets.

per_task.generated_character: Small, heavily fluorinated heterocycles: median 27 heavy atoms, MW 380-400, 3-4 rings, 1-3 aromatic rings, digest halogen_rate 0.9092 and mean SMILES length 46.6, the second shortest of the five. Median fluorine count is 3 per molecule and rises to 4-5 in the top 30. The decisive feature is where the fluorine sits: 74.3 percent of the 870 molecules place a halogen on nitrogen, and that rises to 93-100 percent of the top 30 on seeds 1 and 2. Two cores recur: a xanthine-like fused pyrimidinedione, O=c1c2c(NCCF)n(C3=CC(CF)C=C3O)cc2n(CF)c(=O)n1CF at 0.5992 and COc1cccnc1-n1cc2c(c1C1=CC(F)(F)C1S)c(=N)n(C)c(=O)n2F at 0.6573, and a hydrouracil-type ring carrying a 2-hydroxyphenyl, O=C1C2NC(F)N(c3cc(CCN(F)F)ccc3O)C=C2N(CCF)C(=O)N1F at 0.6584, the digest best.
liabilities: N-F bonds throughout, including N(F)F difluoroamine groups as in O=C1C2NC(F)N(c3cc(CCN(F)F)ccc3O)C=C2N(CCF)C(=O)N1F; these are not isolable amine substituents
alpha-halo amine in 65 percent of seed 2's proposals and 90 percent of its top 30, a built-in alkylating liability
N-Br appearing in late proposals such as O=C1C2NC(F)N(c3cc(CCN(F)Br)ccc3O)CC=C2N(CF)C(=O)N1F
free thiol in 12.1 percent of the set and 63 percent of seed 1's top 30, for example C1=CC(F)(S)C1F
single-atom proposals F, S and O evaluated at the objective floor, 37 molecules under six heavy atoms
missing_features: no trifluoromethyl group in any of the 870 molecules, on the objective whose molecules are the most fluorinated of all five
no polyfluorinated aromatic ring: fluorine is attached to nitrogen in up to 100 percent of the top 30, while aryl halide drops to 0-47 percent there
no defined stereochemistry, although 478 of the task's molecules carry at least one unassigned stereocentre
no secondary amide NH (1.4 percent of the set) and no primary beta-amino carbonyl motif in the high scorers
no saturated six-membered N-heterocycle in the top 30: the saturated nitrogen that is present sits in 4- and 5-membered or fused imide rings
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The gradient clearly rewards more fluorine on a fixed core, and the generator satisfied it the cheapest way available to it. Median heavy atoms stay at 24-29 for the whole run while median block score climbs from 0.003 to 0.527 on seed 2, and the top 30 carry a median of 4-5 fluorines against 3 for the set. Those extra fluorines are added as N-F and as CH2F rather than by building a fluorinated aromatic ring: aryl halide incidence is only 8-64 percent by seed, while N-halogen is 69-78 percent. The digest span is very wide, best 0.6584 against median 0.217213 and a worst of 7.7e-27, because 37 of the 870 molecules are fragments of five heavy atoms or fewer and F, S, O and C#C were each evaluated at the floor. Scores are also brittle at the top: within the last six proposals of seed 2 the score swings from 0.6584 to 0.0910 on what is one N-F substituent of difference.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Across all fifteen trajectory files, 0 of 4350 valid optimizer molecules carry any atom or bond stereo descriptor, matching the digest stereocentre_rate of 0.0 on all five tasks; yet 2540 of those molecules contain at least one unassigned sp3 stereocentre and one contains ten. The sp3-richest sets reach a median of 3-4 unassigned centres per molecule, including every one of the highest-scoring molecules on the sets where fsp3 exceeds 0.45.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator never specifies stereochemistry, although most of what it emits has stereocentres.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Operators would have to set configuration at the sp3 centres they create and inherit a parent's configuration through an edit, so that a stereochemically defined molecule is proposable at all. At present every proposal is a configurational average, so no amount of search can separate two enantiomers and any objective that discriminates them is answered by chance.

transferable_gaps.evidence: No trifluoromethyl group appears in any of the 4350 molecules. On the set with the heaviest halogen load (string-level halogen_rate 0.9092, median 3 fluorines per molecule) 74.3 percent of molecules instead carry a halogen bonded to nitrogen, rising to 93-100 percent of the highest-scoring 30 on two of three sessions, with N(F)F groups in the best molecules. Node-wide, N-halogen appears in 19.3 percent and O-halogen in 2.3 percent of molecules.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator cannot build a polyfluorinated carbon group, and places halogens on heteroatoms instead.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The element-substitution operator should treat multi-halogen carbon groups as single transferable units that can be added or moved intact, and should refuse to place a halogen on nitrogen or oxygen. As it stands, raising halogen count is only reachable through bonds no chemist would draw, so a correct score signal is satisfied by an incorrect structure.

transferable_gaps.evidence: 38.1 percent of the 4350 molecules carry an N-O, N-N, N-S or O-O single bond and 6.5 percent carry a peroxide. This is not confined to low scorers: one session's 30 highest-scoring molecules are 100 percent peroxide-containing, and on another objective 83 percent of a session's top 30 carry an N-O bond while 70 percent of its whole run does. Free thiols appear in 11.9 percent node-wide and 63 percent of one session's top 30.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator freely creates heteroatom-heteroatom single bonds, which dominate its liability profile.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The operator menu needs a bond-pair filter that refuses to join two heteroatoms by a single bond unless that motif arrived intact from a donor fragment that already contained it. Without it, the highest-scoring region the search can reach is populated by structures that are not makeable, so score improvements do not correspond to chemical progress.

transferable_gaps.evidence: On one objective, three sessions of the same optimizer ended at median 72, 41 and 30 heavy atoms. The runaway session grew from a median of 38 heavy atoms at evaluations 11-40 to 110 at evaluations 131-160 while its median score moved only 0.559 to 0.602, and its 30 best molecules average 85 heavy atoms, MW 1136, 10 aromatic rings and QED 0.03. The two sessions that stayed near 30-41 heavy atoms reached higher endpoints on the same objective, so size was not what was being rewarded.
transferable_gaps.gap: Nothing bounds mass accumulation, so one breeding path can ratchet into a size region no medicinal chemistry occupies.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Breeding needs a size or property corridor derived from the live population rather than from the objective, so that crossover cannot keep concatenating whole parents when the score is indifferent to length. A generator that cannot detect its own drift will spend most of a budget in a region where every proposal is unmakeable regardless of what it scores.

transferable_gaps.evidence: 112 of the 4350 molecules have five or fewer heavy atoms and 121 have no ring at all. Single- and two-atom proposals were evaluated on four of the five sets, including F, S, O, C, C#C, NNO, C=CCl, FCl and CCF, and all of them landed at or next to the objective floor. On two sets that is 36 and 37 wasted evaluations out of 870.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator still spends oracle evaluations on degenerate one- and two-atom fragments.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The mutation path should re-draw or repair a proposal that falls below a minimum heavy-atom or ring count before it is announced. These evaluations return no usable gradient to the surrogate and no breeding material, so they are pure budget loss that scales with how often deletion operators fire.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Of the 4350 molecules, piperazine appears in 17, morpholine in 1 and piperidine in 168, while 1455 molecules contain a four-membered ring and the node emits 2030 four-membered rings in total. On the one objective where a ring basic nitrogen dominates the gradient, 100 percent of the 60 highest-scoring molecules carry a basic amine, but the single best molecule reaches it through a spiro N-aryl aziridine (CCC(Cl)c1cc(F)cc(CCCC2CCCN2C23CN2c2cc(Cl)ccc23)c1) and aziridine or azetidine occurs in 100 percent of two sessions' top 30.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator reaches basic nitrogen through strained three- and four-membered rings and cannot produce the common saturated six-membered N-heterocycles.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The donor fragment pool and the ring-construction operator should be able to emit and preserve common saturated six-membered nitrogen rings, and ring closure should be size-weighted away from three- and four-membered rings. The generator's own highest-scoring molecules show it needs a ring basic nitrogen, and it currently buys that feature with a strained ring that destroys the molecule's plausibility.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Digest charged_rate is 0.0 on all five tasks, and node-wide a carboxylic acid appears in 1.15 percent and a sulfonamide in 2.67 percent of 4350 molecules. On one set the acid count is 3 of 870 and the sulfonamide count 1 of 870, while that same set's molecules are otherwise polar heterocycles with median QED 0.56-0.71.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator produces no acidic or ionizable handle, so a whole region of property space is unreachable by construction.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The element and fragment menus need acidic and zwitterion-capable groups as addable units, not only as motifs that survive by accident from the initial pool. A generator that cannot propose one cannot explore the acidic half of property space, and the failure will look like a search failure rather than a representation limit.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every session proposes 290 unique SMILES out of 290 optimizer evaluations, yet on three of the five sets the 30 highest-scoring molecules reduce to only 2-7 unique Murcko scaffolds, against 58-223 distinct scaffolds over the same whole run. The last six proposals of one session are one-substituent variants of a single core whose scores swing from 0.6584 to 0.0910, and on another set best-so-far stops moving after evaluation 221 while eighty further evaluations are spent on the same scaffold.
transferable_gaps.gap: Late search is single-atom churn on one converged core: distinct SMILES without distinct scaffolds.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Parent selection needs a scaffold-level novelty or distance term, because uniqueness at the SMILES level already saturates and therefore cannot signal exploration. A generator whose only late move is a single-site edit will plateau whenever the remaining score is held by the core rather than by the decoration.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
